text: I fell like some of these reviews aren't being honest and they're trying to push a narrative more than honestly review the capabilities of a card. We know that these 8 gb cards often suffer in 1080p games at ultra settings. But how do they perform at low/lowest settings? Without ray tracing. Without upscaling. What does that look like compared to a console? These are basically the lowest or near lowest priced cards you can get and they're geared for lower end systems. DF does have a valid point about the PCIe bandwidth not being enough and they are correct to say that's a poor design choice on Nvidia's part. But the point is while the industry tends to test these GPUs at max everything to show a worst case scenario, we're not seeing the best case scenario and we don't know what that looks like when they only test one way, so we don't know how good they can be either. I wish that reviewers would show that side of it as well. Frank Azor was not wrong when he said that most people game at 1080p and that 8gb IS often enough to provide a smooth experience. Perhaps that comes with the caveat of "when not maxed out" but we don't even know if that's all that bad either. So when we don't get to see that, it's hard for a person to make a fair assessment of a cards overall capability.

​​​​ @jinx20001 Exactly, it all  depends on what games you are mostly going to play, whether it's worth it or not. If you are one of those gamers on a budget who mainly plays on older titles, indie games or are hooked on say a MMO, Online shooter or MOBA, then a 8GB GPU will probably be fine and sufficient enough (at least for now). If however you mostly want a budget GPU to play all of the very latest blockbuster AAA titles (and at high settings), then I would take a very good look elsewhere. Especially at a GPU with more than 8GB of VRAM.
However, the straight up fact is right at the moment, all of the top 20 most played games on PC will all run fine on a 8GB 5060.
BTW, just for reference they are: C2 & 2 & Go, Minecraft, Fortnite, R.E.P.O, Roblox, Sims 4, Dota 2, Schedule I, Leagues of Legends, COD MW2, Valarant, Marvel Rivals, PUBG, Overwatch 1 & 2, GTA5 Online, Rocket League, Apex Legends, TCRS: Siege, Baldur's Gate 3 and Helldivers 2.
BTW, I'm in no way promoting manufacturers to still carry on making 8GB GPU's. They really should have moved on well before now, to at least having a minimum of 12GB of VRAM. However, I'm simply stating that there are still quite a lot of gamers out there who are on a budget and where a 8GB GPU is still more than sufficient for thier needs. And I can also understand them not wanting to fork out extra cash on a 12 or 16GB GPU, when all they ever do is play on Roblox and DOTA 2. Where a 8GB GPU is more than sufficient.
